headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenBBTerminal can ingest MCP/API content while PaddleOCR can process documents/images, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict paths in default pairings.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and FastAPI/REST APIs, so it can ingest external content; PaddleOCR processes documents/images that may contain attacker-controlled text. If OpenBB consumes OCR output as trusted instructions, injection is plausible. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests PaddleOCR output through MCP/API without provenance tagging
IF OCR text is forwarded into an instruction-following prompt or agent loop
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and provenance label before passing OCR text to OpenBBTerminal
Disable automatic instruction-following on OCR outputs
Review one sample OCR-to-agent handoff for prompt-like strings
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking at the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and can use MCP/APIs; PaddleOCR handles documents and images. If they share a workspace or OCR output includes sensitive document text, data can flow from documents into OpenBB outputs. No direct isolation or retention controls are documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or document set
IF OCR output contains financial, licensed, or personal data and is forwarded to OpenBBTerminal
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate directories
Redact sensitive fields before OCR output is shared
Turn off unnecessary logging in the handoff path
Manually inspect one end-to-end sample for leaked fields
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and retention policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal has no filesystem write, git, or shell capability, while PaddleOCR only shows browser and allowlisted egress. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The remaining overlap is mainly API-level coordination, so blast radius is small and low is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external API resource
IF an orchestrator maps OCR output into a shared state store
mitigations: Avoid sharing writable directories between the agents
Use separate API credentials per agent
Serialize access to any shared downstream resource
Check for duplicate writes in one test run

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can transform documents into text, and OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs/MCP inputs. If OCR output is treated as authoritative financial input, errors can cascade into downstream analysis or actions. There is no documented verification step between them, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal uses PaddleOCR output as source data without validation
IF downstream decisions are made from OCR-derived figures or labels
mitigations: Require a human check on OCR-derived numbers before use
Compare OCR output against the source document for one sample
Add schema validation for extracted fields
Flag low-confidence OCR results before ingestion
requires-engineering: add verification and reconciliation logic

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If documents contain regulated financial or personal data, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches, but the profiles do not document a specific jurisdictional breach. Medium is the cautious choice given the data classes involved.
conditions: IF documents processed by PaddleOCR contain regulated financial or personal data
IF OpenBBTerminal stores or logs that data under a different retention policy
mitigations: Minimize logged document content
Separate regulated and non-regulated document flows
Confirm retention settings for both tools
Delete test artifacts after validation
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and subject-rights handling
